messages:
anya: Heads up — p99 latency for hosted/text-generate spiked right after the v8.0 canary expanded to 5% (saw ~2.1x p99). putting here before I start digging.

samir: saw it too. timeline matches canary promotion at ~13:32 UTC. throughput also dipped ~20%.

julien: grabbing traces + profiler now. initial hypothesis: kernel selector flipped to non-quantized path on some hosts.

maria: curious — did tokenizer change in v8.0? I remember a subtoken normalization tweak that can increase avg tokens per request.

julien: yes, tokenizer commit 9f3a7d changed punctuation normalization; average tokens/request jumped from 48 -> 72 on canary traces. seq-len distribution shifted right (heavy tail).

anya: that would interact with KV cache reuse and batching heuristics. longer sequences -> lower batching efficiency and more KV cache misses.

julien: profiler snippet (sampled hot functions, canary host):
```
Kernel: matmul_fused_fp16  time= 8.2ms  (was 4.4ms on baseline)
Kernel: attention_q4_fused time= 2.1ms  (was ~1.9ms)
Batcher: avg_batch_size=3.6  (baseline=6.8)
KV cache hit-rate= 0.72  (baseline=0.94)
```

kai: those numbers scream batching fallout + KV churn. low batch sizes explain the p99 jump. curious why kernel selector took fused_fp16 instead of q4 variant.

samir: I pulled selection logs from two hosts: on noisy-tenant-host-17 selector chose fp16 kernel because predicted peak_mem > 9GB (estimation function overestimates when seq_len > 256). on other hosts it chose q4.

anya: noisy-tenant? any CPU/GPU contention?

infra-bot: host metrics for noisy-tenant-host-17 (13:28-13:40 UTC): GPU utilization=92%, PCIe stalls increased, context-switches spiked + network RX bursts.

maria: suggests neighbor caused memory pressure -> selector hedged to fp16 to avoid OOM, but fp16 kernels are slower for our quantized models.

julien: repro plan: 1) compare kernel selector heuristics with actual allocation during canary 2) simulate seq-len shift on a baseline host to see batching effect 3) check KV cache eviction logs.

samir: I already ran a quick simulation: driving synthetic requests with longer tails reproduced the batcher dropping to median batch_size 3 and p99 increase ~1.9x. KV cache eviction rate increased because more prefixes meant fewer reuse opportunities.

anya: immediate mitigation options? rollback or targeted rollback of tokenizer change in canary? or tune selector to prefer q4 unless OOM risk confirmed?

julien: quick fixes I can push: 1) tighten selector threshold for switching off q4 (decrease safety margin) 2) increase batcher grace window from 10ms -> 20ms on canary hosts to allow slightly larger batches. both are config flags we can flip.

maria: rolling back tokenizer would be safer but slower to enact if we need to coordinate model tests.

deploy-bot: canary rollback for service hosted/text-generate initiated by @maria at 13:53 UTC.

anya: thanks. can we also add a short-term autoscaling/burst rule for noisy-tenant-host-17 to reduce neighbor interference?

infra-bot: created ticket INF-8721 to isolate noisy tenant. suggested immediate soft-isolation: reduce co-located tenant to 30% concurrency.

julien: after flipping selector margin + batcher grace on a test host p99 returned near-baseline in 15m of synthetic load. pushing the config to the other canary hosts now (will monitor).

samir: after the rollback + selector tweak we've seen p99 drop back ~1.05x of baseline. KV hit-rate recovering (0.9). throughput back to within 5% of baseline.

anya: write up for postmortem: root cause = tokenizer change increased token lengths -> interacted with conservative kernel selection + batching heuristic leading to small batches + KV cache reuse reduction. noisy neighbor amplified selector conservatism on some hosts. mitigation: revert tokenizer in canary, adjust selector thresholds, extend batcher grace, and ticket to isolate noisy tenant.

maria: noted — I'll open the rollout hold/rollback checklist and add test to detect avg tokens/request drift in future canaries.

julien: adding follow-ups: (a) instrument kernel selector decisions in more detail (why it chose path X), (b) add a pre-rollout metric asserting avg tokens per request delta < 10%, (c) KV cache eviction alert.

anya: thanks all. I'll draft the incident thread for the postmortem and link INF-8721 + the rollback PR. :thumbsup:
